fact_text: The global textile market is put at roughly $850-900 billion a year, with the United States alone a market of about $150-200 billion, according to the APTMA chairman.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Pakistan's textile exports were $17.8 billion in FY25, close to 2% of global textile trade, the APTMA chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Pakistan's total exports rose to about $30-32 billion in FY25, with textiles providing the lion's share of that gain, the chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Pakistan's textile exports reached about $19.3 billion around 2022, fell to about $16.5-16.6 billion, and recovered to $17.8 billion in FY25, the chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Bangladesh's textile exports were about $47-50 billion over the same period, and Bangladesh is targeting $60 billion, according to the chairman.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman put shares of global textile trade at about 35% for China, 6.5% for Bangladesh and 3.5-4% for India, with Pakistan near 2%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Over about 15 years Pakistan's textile exports moved from yarn and grey fabric toward value-added products such as home textiles, denim, knitted fabrics and sports socks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Exporters cannot export domestic inflation, so Pakistani input costs must be benchmarked against Vietnam, Bangladesh, India, China and Sri Lanka, and a higher local cost base creates difficulties.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman named three levers for regional competitiveness: electricity tariffs, interest rates and taxation, which he said APTMA cannot change alone and which require state decisions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: APTMA's patron-in-chief, Dr Gohar Ejaz, introduced the idea of regionally competitive energy tariffs, which the association asks for without seeking subsidies, the chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The industrial power tariff carried a cross-subsidy of about Rs 250 billion, of which Rs 100 billion was removed around 2023 and about Rs 140-150 billion remains, the chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: APTMA's proposal is that the state stop collecting the cross-subsidy from industrial tariffs and move the money into the PSDP or another support programme, so industry is not billed for other sectors' losses.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman estimated that removing the industrial cross-subsidy could cut the power tariff by about Rs 6-8 per unit, which he said would let industry compete again.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said bulk power to B3 and B4 industrial feeders has line losses close to zero and is paid on time, so unnecessary cost is low on those feeders.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said large-scale power theft on metered single-point B3 and B4 industrial feeders is almost impossible, so only small-scale theft is possible.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: After gas and furnace oil were withdrawn from industry, many textile members moved to solar, solar-battery and wind, the chairman said, to reduce dependence on the government grid.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman expects battery prices to fall to about a quarter of their 2025 level within three to four years, which would make off-grid solar cheaper for textile mills.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Punjab mills mainly combine grid, solar and solar-battery systems because large wind corridors are not near industrial zones there, while Sindh and Karachi mills can also use wind.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: According to the chairman, APTMA membership starts at a turnover of about 1 billion (currency not stated) and the rest are large corporate entities.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: APTMA said it engages the federal government on power, gas, cotton, taxation and SIFC matters more than in the past, and it raises issues with the IMF, prime minister and finance ministry.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: APTMA, FPCCI and PCGA joined an action plan with SIFC to save cotton, bringing in the Kisan Ittehad for the first time, the chairman said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The government lifted a 50-year-old ban on cotton seed imports, and the chairman expects cotton farming to return in Cholistan with Chinese support, then spread across the country.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said cotton can be saved if farmers are taught timely spraying and told to use only standardised seed, and he credited the Green Pakistan Initiative with focusing on cotton.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman estimated the cotton-to-garment chain could add $25-30 billion in exports in the short run and at least $40-50 billion in the long run.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Pakistan has a full vertical textile chain from cotton farming through ginning, spinning, weaving, dyeing, finishing and garmenting, which the chairman said Bangladesh has also built.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said the $7 billion IMF programme imposed heavy conditions on the whole nation, and that textile exports could replace that financing if they rise.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said textiles could add $7-8 billion in exports within two to four years if the state gave competitive power, interest rates and taxation, a gain he framed as a simple quick fix.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The FBR's FY26 tax target is Rs 14 trillion, against an FY25 target of Rs 13.2 trillion and actual collection of about Rs 12-12.2 trillion, the interviewer and chairman noted.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said many companies and individuals stay outside the tax net, and that documenting the black economy and enforcing tax law is the state's job, not the industry's.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman argued that full tax collection could remove the need for IMF, World Bank or ADB financing, but he framed the revenue potential without a clear figure.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The interviewer cited a government energy plan for 2025-2035 aimed at enhancing electricity generation, and the chairman said industry has not seen that support in practice.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman argued that textile subsidies ended around 2021-2022, and that high power, gas and interest costs, not subsidies, explain why the sector did not grow to its potential.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said gas and power taken illegally in restricted areas is causing large bills, which he said ultimately fall on the government or the public, and that APTMA does not back members caught stealing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The interviewee acknowledged that some firms compromise on quality and technology and overstate their workforce, while saying such firms are a small part of the sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: Most Pakistani cargo leaves Karachi on feeder vessels for transshipment at Dubai, Salalah or Oman, where it is moved onto mother vessels, which adds cost and time.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said Gwadar, a deep-sea port, should be made fully functional, and that dredging Karachi and Port Qasim channels would let mother vessels call, saving shipping lines large costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said shipping from Karachi to Hong Kong can be cheaper than moving goods inland to upcountry, so internal logistics costs and freight rates need study.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman noted Pakistan is the world's fifth most populous country, which he said gives the domestic market depth and room for taxes to be collected more widely.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)

fact_text: The chairman said about two in every five garments in major stores abroad are made in Bangladesh, which he presented as that country's success.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'APTMA Chairman Explains Why Pakistan’s Textile Industry Needs Urgent Reform | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-10-14)
